definitionEn: a strong belief or opinion that you feel certain is right
senseNote: Also 'being found guilty in court' (a criminal conviction); here — a strong personal belief.
situation: Someone holds a strong personal belief and feels certain enough about it to act or argue accordingly.

examples.text: Despite fierce criticism, the CEO spoke with real [[conviction]] about the company's new direction.
She left her well-paid job because of a deep [[conviction]] that teaching mattered more.
Even under cross-examination, the witness never wavered in her [[conviction]] that she had seen the accused.

texts: He has always acted according to his political [[conviction]].
Her voice was full of quiet [[conviction]] as she described the plan.
There is a growing [[conviction]] among scientists that the treatment works.

badCollocation.noteRu: Убеждение не make, а form или hold: form a conviction, hold strong convictions.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчивое выражение — the courage of your convictions (смелость действовать по своим убеждениям). Decisions, achievements и instincts в нём не используются.

nuance.text: His [[conviction]] that nuclear power is essential has never changed in thirty years.
nuance.explanationRu: Conviction — твёрдое, устойчивое убеждение, за которое человек готов бороться. Opinion — просто мнение, которое легко меняют; здесь важна именно неизменность взгляда за 30 лет.

reverse.text: I'd like to hear your [[opinion]] on the new restaurant before we book it.
reverse.explanationRu: О ресторане высказывают лёгкое мнение — opinion. Conviction — слишком сильное слово для повседневных предпочтений вроде выбора ресторана.

fixIt.text: Despite strong opposition, he never lost his [[persuasion]] that the treaty was necessary.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Убеждение» как твёрдая вера — conviction. Persuasion — это процесс убеждения кого-то, а не сама устойчивая вера человека.

wordFormation.text: Losing the argument did nothing to shake his [[conviction]] that he was right.

reply.context: In a meeting, your manager asks: "Are you sure this strategy is the right one?"
options: Yes, I have a strong conviction that it will work, based on the data.
Yes, I have a conviction of two years for the strategy.
Yeah, totally, I've got a real gut conviction about it, you know?
reply.explanationRu: Conviction — твёрдая уверенность в правоте; после него используют that-предложение. Второй ответ путает со значением «судимость», третий слишком разговорный для совещания.

rewrite.original: He was completely sure that the plan would succeed, and nothing could change his mind.
rewrite.frame: He had an unshakeable ____ that the plan would succeed.
rewrite.explanationRu: Твёрдая, непоколебимая уверенность — an unshakeable conviction.

definitionEn: to help an official investigation or authority by doing what is asked
senseNote: Also the general sense 'to work together' (children learn to cooperate); here — to help police or an official inquiry.
situation: Someone being questioned by the police or investigators agrees to answer questions and give them information.

examples.text: The suspect finally agreed to [[cooperate]] with detectives after his lawyer advised him to.
Company executives were told to [[cooperate]] fully with the tax inspectors or risk heavy fines.
Staff were asked to [[cooperate]] with the safety review by reporting any hazards they noticed.

texts: Witnesses who refuse to [[cooperate]] can be summoned to court.
The company promised to [[cooperate]] with regulators investigating the leak.
He was warned that failing to [[cooperate]] could lead to further charges.

badCollocation.noteRu: После cooperate используется предлог with, а не to: cooperate with the police.

collocationTask.prompt: The witness agreed to cooperate ___ the investigation.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Cooperate требует предлога with: cooperate with the police/investigation. To, for и at здесь не подходят.

nuance.text: The bank had to [[cooperate]] with regulators by handing over its internal records.
nuance.explanationRu: Cooperate — активно помогать, включая предоставление информации по своей инициативе; comply — просто подчиняться требованию. Здесь банк сам передаёт документы, помогая следствию.

reverse.text: Drivers must [[comply]] with the new speed limit or face a fine.
reverse.explanationRu: Соблюдать формальное правило — comply with a rule/law. Cooperate предполагает активную помощь человеку или расследованию, а не просто следование правилам.

fixIt.text: After the accident, all staff were told to [[collaborate]] with the investigators and answer every question.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Сотрудничать с полицией/следствием» — cooperate with. Collaborate обычно про совместную творческую или научную работу, а иногда звучит как «пособничество».

wordFormation.text: Better [[cooperation]] between the two departments could prevent mistakes like this.

reply.context: A friend texts: "The neighbours reported our noisy party to the council. What should we do now?"
options: We should cooperate the council about the noise complaint.
I think we should just cooperate and turn the music down if they ask.
We shall endeavour to cooperate fully with the municipal authorities forthwith.
reply.explanationRu: Cooperate требует предлога with: cooperate with the council. Первый вариант грамматически неверен, третий — слишком официален для сообщения другу.

rewrite.original: The company promised to help the police with their inquiry in every way possible.
rewrite.frame: The company promised to ____ fully with the police.
rewrite.explanationRu: Помогать в расследовании, отвечая на вопросы, — cooperate with the police.

definitionEn: willing to help and do what is asked, especially in an official or difficult situation
senseNote: Also the everyday sense 'helpful and easy to work with' (a cooperative child); here — willing to help and comply, especially with officials or during a difficult process.
situation: A person, company or country agrees to help and follow requests during an investigation, negotiation or difficult process.

examples.text: The airline was surprisingly [[cooperative]] once passengers threatened to complain publicly.
Investigators said the company had been fully [[cooperative]] throughout the inquiry.
Union leaders praised staff for staying [[cooperative]] during the difficult restructuring process.

texts: The witness remained [[cooperative]] throughout the long interview.
Local farmers were generally [[cooperative]] when the new regulations were explained.
Neither side was particularly [[cooperative]] during the ceasefire talks.

badCollocation.noteRu: После cooperative нужен предлог with, а не to: cooperative with the police.

collocationTask.prompt: Were the passengers cooperative ___ the crew during the delay?
collocationTask.explanationRu: Cooperative требует предлога with: cooperative with someone. To, of и for здесь не подходят.

nuance.text: The tenants were [[cooperative]], suggesting several solutions of their own during the meeting.
nuance.explanationRu: Cooperative — активно помогает и предлагает своё, compliant — просто выполняет требования, не проявляя инициативы. Здесь жильцы сами предлагают решения.

reverse.text: Employees are simply expected to be [[compliant]] with the new dress code, whether they like it or not.
reverse.explanationRu: Просто подчиняться правилу, без вопроса согласия, — compliant. Cooperative подразумевает активную помощь и добрую волю, которых здесь нет.

fixIt.text: After the crash, the airline's staff were very [[corporate]] about arranging refunds and hotel rooms for passengers.
fixIt.explanationRu: Corporate — «корпоративный, относящийся к компании», а не «готовый помочь». Готовность помогать и содействовать — cooperative.

wordFormation.text: Negotiators were relieved to find the union far more [[cooperative]] than expected.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "How did the meeting with the auditors go?"
options: Really well, the auditors were very cooperative-looking, very smart suits.
Splendid! The auditory personnel demonstrated exemplary cooperation throughout the proceedings.
Really well, actually — everyone was very cooperative and answered all their questions.
reply.explanationRu: Cooperative описывает поведение, а не внешность. Первый ответ бессмысленно использует его для описания одежды, второй звучит слишком официально для разговора с коллегой.

rewrite.original: The company answered every question the investigators asked without any resistance.
rewrite.frame: The company was extremely ____ during the investigation.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Не сопротивлялась, отвечала на все вопросы» = was cooperative.

definitionEn: to organise people or activities so that they work well together
senseNote: Also 'to match well together' about colours or clothes (the curtains coordinate with the sofa); here — to organise people or actions so they work well together.
situation: Someone makes sure that several people, teams or activities work together smoothly towards the same goal.

examples.text: The charity needed someone to [[coordinate]] deliveries between the warehouse and dozens of local shelters.
Emergency services had to [[coordinate]] their response after the bridge collapsed.
As project manager, she [[coordinates]] the work of five different design teams.

texts: Someone needs to [[coordinate]] the volunteers before Saturday's event.
The two departments rarely [[coordinate]] their schedules, which causes confusion.
NGOs are working together to [[coordinate]] aid efforts in the region.

badCollocation.noteRu: Для одной простой встречи говорят arrange или make an appointment. Coordinate — согласовывать действия нескольких людей или сторон.

collocationTask.prompt: Firefighters had to ___ closely with police during the rescue.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Согласовывать действия с другими службами — coordinate with. Obey, announce и apologise сюда не подходят по смыслу.

nuance.text: A control room [[coordinates]] the movements of every ambulance in the city.
nuance.explanationRu: Coordinate — активно организовывать и распределять действия разных сторон. Cooperate — просто соглашаться помогать, без функции организатора. Диспетчерская именно управляет.

reverse.text: Local residents happily [[cooperated]] with police by locking their cars overnight.
reverse.explanationRu: Просто согласиться помочь — cooperate. Coordinate предполагает активное управление и распределение задач, а не просто отдельную помощь.

fixIt.text: The two hospitals now [[correlate]] their emergency schedules to avoid gaps in coverage.
fixIt.explanationRu: Correlate — быть статистически связанным (a и b correlate). Согласовывать расписания и действия людей или служб — coordinate.

wordFormation.text: Good [[coordination]] between the fire service and the hospital made the difference.

reply.context: Your manager says: "Three different teams are all planning leaflet drops in the same neighbourhood next week."
options: We should get someone to coordinate the teams into more leaflets.
One must endeavour to coordinate the disparate scheduling arrangements forthwith.
We should get someone to coordinate the schedules so they don't overlap.
reply.explanationRu: Coordinate the schedules — согласовать расписания, чтобы не пересекались. Первый вариант звучит неестественно, второй слишком официален для разговора с руководителем.

rewrite.original: Someone needs to make sure the three departments don't schedule events on the same day.
rewrite.frame: Someone needs to ____ the departments' schedules.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Согласовать, чтобы не пересекались» — coordinate the schedules.

definitionEn: the ability to make different parts of your body move together smoothly and accurately
senseNote: Also 'the organisation of people or plans so that they work well together' (coordination between departments); here — smooth control of body movements.
situation: A doctor, coach or teacher notices how smoothly and accurately someone can move and control different parts of their body.

examples.text: Years of playing the piano gave her excellent hand-eye [[coordination]].
After the stroke, he had to relearn basic hand [[coordination]] through physiotherapy.
The dance instructor said my footwork lacked [[coordination]], so I kept missing the beat.

texts: The injury affected his balance and [[coordination]] for several months.
Good [[coordination]] is essential for gymnasts and dancers alike.
The test measures memory, reaction time and physical [[coordination]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Координацию не make, а have, develop или improve: improve your coordination.

collocationTask.prompt: Playing the drums from a young age really improved his ___.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Ловкость и согласованность движений — coordination. Attendance, punctuality и politeness к физическим навыкам не относятся.

nuance.text: Juggling three balls at once takes real [[coordination]], not just quick hands.
nuance.explanationRu: Coordination — согласованная работа разных частей тела (руки, глаза). Balance — умение не терять равновесие; жонглирование требует именно координации.

reverse.text: She practises yoga every morning to improve her [[balance]] and flexibility.
reverse.explanationRu: Умение не падать, сохранять равновесие — balance. Coordination — согласованность движений разных частей тела, а не устойчивость.

fixIt.text: Her poor hand-eye [[balance]] made it hard for her to catch the ball.
fixIt.explanationRu: Проблема с ловлей мяча — это hand-eye coordination (согласованность глаз и рук), а не balance (равновесие, чтобы не упасть).

wordFormation.text: Swimming well requires excellent [[coordination]] between your arms and legs.

reply.context: A friend says: "I tried the new dance class yesterday and it was a disaster."
options: Ha, don't worry — coordination between the two of you will improve the class.
Ha, don't worry — coordination like that takes practice for everyone at first.
One's motor coordination invariably requires considerable practice to attain proficiency.
reply.explanationRu: Здесь coordination — согласованность движений тела. Первый вариант путает со значением «согласование действий между людьми», третий звучит как выдержка из учебника.

definitionEn: a person whose job is to organise an activity so that everyone involved works well together
situation: Someone's official job is to plan an event or project and make sure everyone involved works well together.

examples.text: As the volunteer [[coordinator]], she matches people's skills to the tasks that need doing.
The wedding [[coordinator]] arrived early to check that every supplier knew the schedule.
Our new safety [[coordinator]] runs fire drills and checks the emergency exits every month.

texts: The event [[coordinator]] sent everyone the final schedule last night.
She works as a [[coordinator]] for an international aid charity.
The hospital hired a new patient-care [[coordinator]] this month.

badCollocation.noteRu: Правильно coordinator of/for a project, а не on: the coordinator of the new project.

collocationTask.prompt: The charity is looking for a ___ to organise volunteers and match their skills to tasks.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Тот, кто согласовывает работу волонтёров, — coordinator. Donor, patron и spokesperson называют совсем другие роли.

nuance.text: As [[coordinator]], her role was to connect the different teams, not to manage their budgets.
nuance.explanationRu: Coordinator согласовывает работу разных людей или отделов, но обычно не имеет над ними формальной власти. Manager — руководитель, который отвечает за результат.

reverse.text: As store [[manager]], he is responsible for every employee's performance and pay.
reverse.explanationRu: Формальная власть над сотрудниками и их зарплатой — это manager. Coordinator согласовывает работу, но обычно не руководит подчинёнными напрямую.

fixIt.text: The company employed an events [[administrator]] to make sure every supplier and venue worked to the same timetable.
fixIt.explanationRu: Тот, кто согласовывает работу поставщиков и площадок под одно расписание, — coordinator. Administrator обычно ведёт документы, а не объединяет разных людей вокруг общей задачи.

wordFormation.text: The charity's new [[coordinator]] starts work on Monday.

rewrite.original: A person was hired whose job is to make sure every team works well together on the new product launch.
rewrite.frame: The company hired a ____ for the new product launch.
rewrite.explanationRu: Человек, который следит, чтобы все команды работали слаженно, — a coordinator.

definitionEn: an informal British word for a police officer
senseNote: Also the metal 'copper' (copper wire); here — an informal British word for a police officer.
situation: In informal British English, someone talks about a police officer in a casual, everyday way.

examples.text: A [[copper]] on the corner waved the traffic through after the accident.
Two [[coppers]] knocked on our door asking about the break-in next door.
My uncle was a [[copper]] for thirty years before he retired.

texts: The [[copper]] took down every detail in his notebook.
She's dating a [[copper]] from the local station.
Even the [[copper]] admitted the fine seemed a bit harsh.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Страж закона» по-английски — an officer of the law (более официально). С разговорным copper этот оборот не используют.

collocationTask.prompt: Everyone scattered when they saw the ___ coming down the street.
collocationTask.explanationRu: В разговорном британском английском полицейского называют a copper. Mayor, vicar и librarian — другие профессии, к этой ситуации не подходят.

nuance.text: The [[copper]] on the beat radioed for backup as soon as he saw the fight.
nuance.explanationRu: Copper — разговорное слово для обычного патрульного полицейского. Detective — следователь в штатском, который расследует дела, а не патрулирует улицы.

reverse.text: A [[detective]] spent months piecing together evidence before the arrest.
reverse.explanationRu: Расследованием дел месяцами занимается detective. Copper — неформальное слово для обычного постового полицейского, а не следователя.

fixIt.text: A [[corporal]] stopped us for speeding just outside the village.
fixIt.explanationRu: Corporal — воинское звание (капрал), а не полицейский. Полицейского в разговорном британском английском называют a copper.

reply.context: A friend texts: "Why were you so late last night?"
options: Ha, I stopped to fix a copper pipe under the sink.
Ha, I was apprehended by a police constable regarding a defective vehicular light.
Ha, a copper pulled me over for a broken tail light.
reply.explanationRu: Здесь copper — полицейский (разговорное брит.). В первом ответе имеется в виду медь (металл), во втором — слишком официальный стиль для переписки с другом.

definitionEn: the legal right to control who may copy, publish or use a creative work
senseNote: The basic idea is just knowing that copying is against the law; here we look at the fuller sense — who owns, holds or transfers this right.
situation: A writer, musician or company owns the legal right to decide who may copy or use their creative work.

examples.text: The photographer still owns the [[copyright]] on every picture he has ever taken.
Uploading the whole film without permission is a clear breach of [[copyright]].
The publisher renewed the [[copyright]] before the original term expired.

texts: The song's [[copyright]] belongs to the original composer, not the singer.
Photos on this website are protected by [[copyright]].
The book's [[copyright]] expired decades ago, so anyone can now publish it freely.

badCollocation.noteRu: Авторское право не take, а hold, own или register: hold the copyright, register a copyright.

collocationTask.prompt: Who ___ the copyright to this photograph?
collocationTask.explanationRu: Владеть авторским правом — hold the copyright. Make, give и spend с copyright не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The novel's [[copyright]] protects the text itself, not just the title.
nuance.explanationRu: Copyright защищает само произведение — текст, музыку, фильм. Trademark — это защита названия, логотипа или бренда, а не содержания книги.

reverse.text: The company registered its logo as a [[trademark]] to stop competitors copying it.
reverse.explanationRu: Логотип и название бренда защищает trademark. Copyright защищает содержание творческой работы, а не сам логотип.

fixIt.text: As the author, she automatically owns the [[patent]] on her novel the moment she finishes writing it.
fixIt.explanationRu: Права на литературное произведение — copyright, он возникает автоматически. Patent защищает технические изобретения, а не текст книги.

reply.context: A colleague says: "Can I just use this stock photo from Google Images in our brochure?"
options: Better check first — it might still be under a copyright of ten years.
Better check first — it might still be under copyright.
One must ascertain whether said image remains subject to extant copyright protections.
reply.explanationRu: «Защищено авторским правом» — under copyright, без лишних уточнений. Первый вариант звучит неестественно, третий — как юридический документ.
